title: Clare's sisters
hookLine: enclosed, poor and joyful, praying for the world

cards: Night in Assisi. A young woman from a noble family slips out of her father's house, by a side door, tradition says, and hurries down the hill to the little church where Francis and his brothers live.
They meet her with torches. There, before the altar, she lays aside her fine clothes, and Francis cuts off her hair. Her name is Clare, and this path met her early on.

Soon after, at the convent where Francis has sent her, her family comes to bring her home, and she holds on to the altar and won't let go. Today, the women who followed her, and the hidden life they chose.

teach.h: POVERTY: THE PRIVILEGE OF OWNING NOTHING.
teach.b: Clare settles at San Damiano, the small church Francis had rebuilt with his own hands. Other women join her, her own sister among them, and they become the Poor Ladies, known today as the Poor Clares.

Their life has three marks. The first is poverty, and Clare holds on to it fiercely. Her early biography says a pope once offered to free her from her vow of poverty, so the sisters could own property and be secure.
She told him she never wanted to be freed from following Christ. What she asked for instead was a privilege: the right to own nothing at all. The second mark is enclosure.

The sisters stay inside the monastery walls; visitors speak to them through a grille, and the world mostly goes on without seeing them. To an outside eye that can look like hiding. Clare saw it as making room.
Jesus says in the gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, "enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret."

The enclosure is a whole life lived behind that shut door. The third mark is one an outsider might not expect: joy. Clare's letters to Agnes of Prague, a princess who chose the same life, are full of it.
She tells Agnes to gaze into Christ as into a mirror, every day, and to see herself there.

teach.h: PRAYING FOR A WORLD THAT DOESN'T SEE.
teach.b: And Poor Clares pray for the world outside, for people who'll never know their names.

teach.h: PRAY TO THY FATHER IN SECRET.
teach.b: Hidden, in their tradition, doesn't mean absent. It means close by, unseen, holding things up.

how: Poor Clare monasteries live in enclosure and pray the Liturgy of the Hours through the day, and some Catholics send them prayer requests by letter or leave them at the monastery door.

games.q: you're Clare. a pope offers to free you from your vow of poverty, so your sisters can own property and be secure. what do you say?
o: accept a little land, but nothing more.
say you never want to be freed from following Christ.
games.why: her early biography says she refused, and asked instead for the privilege of owning nothing.

practice: Somewhere right now, behind a wall you'll never walk through, sisters are at prayer; you don't know their names, and they don't know yours. Hold them in mind, and anyone who quietly keeps others in prayer.
If you pray, pray for them; if you don't, send them your thanks into the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Poor Clares. The sisters who follow Saint Clare: poor, enclosed, joyful, praying for a world that rarely sees them. Today's word.
